notes: I refined definitions, added exclusion rules to clarify adjacent labels and reduce ambiguity, sharpened examples for clarity, and maintained the original codebook structure while improving overall precision.

codes.name: access barriers
codes.definition: Structural obstacles that physically prevent access to care, such as distance, transport, or scheduling limitations.
codes.clarification: Include any obstacle that directly hinders a patient's ability to reach care.
codes.negative_clarification: NOT cost concerns; separate issues of affordability and financial burden from physical barriers.

positive_examples.text: A rural clinic is two hours away, requiring an entire day of work to get there.
positive_examples.why: Distance and transport physically block reaching care.

negative_examples.text: The waiting room was crowded and I had to wait for three hours.
negative_examples.why: A logistical issue (wait times), not about physical barriers.

exclusion_rules: Wait times are separate from access barriers; exclude scheduling-related issues

codes.name: cost concerns
codes.definition: The worry or fear of the financial cost of care, including bills, copays, premiums, and debt.
codes.clarification: Include any mention of affordability, insurance not covering enough, or skipping care due to money concerns.
codes.negative_clarification: NOT difficulty physically reaching care; focus on financial burden, not access barriers.

codes.name: provider trust
codes.definition: The patient's confidence in their clinician's expertise and judgment, as well as the overall credibility of the healthcare system.
codes.clarification: Include feeling heard or dismissed, doubting a diagnosis, or relying on a provider's guidance.
codes.negative_clarification: NOT general satisfaction with logistics like wait times; this is about the relationship and trust in the provider.

positive_examples.text: My doctor never listens to me, so I've started questioning their expertise.
positive_examples.why: Expresses distrust in the provider relationship.

negative_examples.text: The clinic's website is easy to navigate and provide clear information on wait times.
negative_examples.why: A logistics complaint (wait times), not about trust in the provider.

exclusion_rules: Wait times are separate from provider trust; exclude scheduling-related issues

codes.name: wait times
codes.definition: The delay between seeking care and receiving it, including appointment lead time or time spent waiting on the day.
codes.clarification: Include long lead times for appointments and in-clinic waits, but separate from access barriers.
codes.negative_clarification: NOT being unable to reach the clinic at all (that is an access barrier); wait times assume care is reachable but slow.

positive_examples.text: The first available appointment was four months out, and I had to schedule it three weeks in advance.
positive_examples.why: A direct delay in receiving care.

negative_examples.text: There's no specialist within a hundred miles of me.
negative_examples.why: Care is unreachable, an access barrier, not merely delayed.

exclusion_rules: Access barriers are separate from wait times; exclude scheduling-related issues
